| 072-claude | P02/P45-family handoff: halve every residual-stream write (emb, attention proj, fc2) after pretraining, a function-preserving rescale | claude-opus-5-5 | init, optimizer | 0.3 | 1200/300/4 | 14 | 344 | 753 | discard | 0.988 | 0.0915 | 92 273 601 761 | 1073 | P02 follow-up handoff transform: halving every residual-stream write (emb, proj, fc2 weights+biases; RESID_SCALE 0.5) after the unchanged 070-claude pretraining scored 370/350/311 on seeds 0/1/2 versus 359/335/364: exact means 343.666667 versus 352.666667, -9.00 (-2.6%); paired +11/+15/-53. Discard; inside the registered -40 to +30 range. The rescale was NOT function-preserving in practice, which falsifies the registered drift prediction (<1e-2): the logged max \|logit drift\| on the first 128 val records was 1.68/1.61/2.05. The probe includes pad positions and does not separate them from real tokens, so where the drift sits is unmeasured. Leading (untested) suspect is LayerNorm eps 1e-5: halving the residual stream makes eps 4x larger relative to its variance, most at block 0's ln1 (embedding rows only) and at pad positions whose embedding never gets gradient. The drift hurt the start: round-1 targets 92/284/102 vs 200/324/206, round-1 sample acc 0.019/0.094/0.021 vs 070's 0.059 (s0) and 0.129 (s1). Pretraining itself matched 070: 4747/4754/4738 steps, final val loss 0.0915/0.0923/0.0942 vs 0.0911/0.0913/0.0961. RL then caught up fast, consistent with (but not proof of) higher RL plasticity. Targets went 92->273->601->761 on s0 (round-4 acc 0.435/0.474/0.395 vs 0.464/0.460/0.485) and RL-solved was 761/807/690 vs 788/783/838. Seeds 0/1 beat 070 on dev at every length (s0 ge 7/8/9/10 = 370/302/221/30 vs 359/281/201/20) and seed 2 did not recover (690 RL-solved, ge>=10 9 vs 27). Post-RL held-out greedy 0.988/0.9905/0.989 vs 0.987/0.987/0.9875. Totals 1073/1055/994 s vs 1048/971/1079, no timing cost. So this run confounds a damaged start with extra plasticity and cannot isolate the mechanism. Next: an exact version that also sets every LayerNorm's eps to eps*RESID_SCALE^2 at handoff (then the rescale is exact), checking drift on non-pad positions only before launch. |

| 076-claude | P23-family: squared-ReLU MLP activation (Primer) instead of GELU, parameter-identical | claude-opus-5-5 | architecture | 0.3 | 1200/300/4 | 14 | 320 | 769 | discard | 0.9825 | 0.0945 | 172 339 631 763 | 1079 | P23-family: squared-ReLU MLP, fc2(relu(fc1(h))^2), on the 070-claude incumbent scored 297/323/339 on seeds 0/1/2 versus 359/335/364: exact means 319.67 versus 352.67, -33.0 (-9.4%); paired -62/-12/-25. Discard; inside the registered -40 to +30 range but far below the central +3. The registered step prediction failed: pretraining ran only 3620/3657/3647 steps versus 070's 4784/4750/4776 (-24%, ~1.31x step time). Most likely cause (not profiled): relu and square are two unfused elementwise passes, with an extra saved intermediate, over the 128 x T x 1024 MLP hidden tensor where GELU is one fused kernel, and at d_model 256 these memory-bound ops are a large share of each step. Despite 24% fewer steps, final val loss matched 070 (0.0945/0.0908/0.0933 vs 0.0911/0.0913/0.0961; means 0.0929 vs 0.0928), so per step relu^2 learned faster, as in Primer, but per wall-clock second it bought nothing, and downstream RL was worse at matched val loss: RL-solved 763/762/781 vs 788/783/838, round-4 sample acc 0.434/0.435/0.463 vs 0.464/0.460/0.485. Sampling speed was not the problem: total seconds 1065/971/1079 vs 1048/971/1079, no timeout risk realized. The result confounds the activation with 24% fewer optimizer steps; separating them needs a fused relu^2 (e.g. a compiled MLP), and the matched-val-loss/worse-RL pattern means that is worth doing only if the step-time cost can be removed. |

The +48 exceeds the stated -25..+30 range; with one-seed sd ~44 part of it is likely luck. Two mechanisms are confounded here: the more uniform update spectrum (singular values ~[0.86,1.14] vs ~[0.68,1.13]) and a ~15% larger update RMS, which under the lr-coupled 10x decoupled decay also shifts the equilibrium weight norm. An RMS-matched control (Polar Express with MUON_LR / 1.15, or the old quintic scaled x1.15) would separate them. |
